criterion: EDI releases in, ASNs and invoices out (830, 862, 856, 810)
why: NetSuite and Business Central have no EDI engine of their own and rely on a third-party service. Kinetic has an EDI and demand management module, though one automotive customer added a partner product on top of it. Plex sells EDI as part of the same platform.

This is where automotive differs most from general manufacturing. NetSuite and Business Central get there through partner work. Kinetic handles release schedules in demand management; how well it reconciles CUMs is my judgment. Plex has sold release accounting for over ten years.

Plex tracks stock by labeled container as part of how it works (my judgment, not sourced). Kinetic prints labels, but the customer in S11 added a partner product to meet automotive label rules. The other two need an add-on.

criterion: Lot and heat traceability, steel coil to shipped part
why: All four track lots without add-ons. Plex scores higher because production and inventory share one database, so the trail from coil to container needs no stitching together.

NetSuite's quality module is a SuiteApp that a NetSuite consultancy calls basic. Business Central only got built-in inspections in April 2026. Kinetic has quality assurance in the core product and a separate QMS. Plex includes a QMS.

criterion: PPAP and APQP, control plans, gauge calibration
why: NetSuite partners set up PPAP on top of the quality SuiteApp. Business Central's new module covers inspections only. Kinetic covers PPAP and APQP documents through Epicor QMS, a separate product. Plex's coverage of gauges and control plans is my judgment.

criterion: MRP driven by customer release demand
why: All four run MRP. In NetSuite and Business Central the release demand has to arrive through the EDI add-on first, which is one more thing to keep in step.

criterion: Finite scheduling of presses and weld cells
why: Kinetic lists infinite, finite and constraint-based scheduling plus an advanced planning module. Plex has constraint-based scheduling. NetSuite users often add a scheduling SuiteApp. Business Central's score is my judgment: finite scheduling there usually means a partner product.

Plex's MES is part of the ERP. Kinetic has data collection built in and sells an advanced MES module. NetSuite has a mobile app for production reporting but consultancies list shop-floor data collection as an integration. Business Central's score is my judgment.

Die life and press maintenance matter in a stamping plant. Plex and Kinetic both sell maintenance as part of their own suites. NetSuite partners list asset maintenance as SuiteApp territory. Business Central's score is my judgment.
No real difference. All four handle bin locations and scanning with their own warehouse features.

criterion: General ledger, payables, receivables and month-end close
why: NetSuite started as an accounting system and it shows. Plex was built from the shop floor up. That its finance is thinner than the others is my judgment.

criterion: Standard cost and variance by part
why: Kinetic's roots are in job costing for manufacturers. NetSuite's costing is fine for simple routings and thinner once labor and overhead need to be split by operation.
NetSuite's saved searches and Business Central with Power BI are both stronger for a controller building their own reports than what Kinetic or Plex ship with.
A third-party comparison marks procurement as a weaker area for Plex. The other three are my judgment.

NetSuite, Business Central and Plex are cloud products with upgrades handled by the vendor. Kinetic runs in the cloud, on premise or both, and its newer screens do not yet cover everything the older client did.
Business Central sits inside Microsoft's platform, which a two-person IT team can do a lot with. Kinetic has REST services. Plex's score is my judgment.
NetSuite, Business Central and Kinetic each have their own tools for adding fields, forms and workflows. Plex is more fixed.
No meaningful difference that I could find.

criterion: Automotive suppliers of this size already using it
why: Plex was designed by an auto supplier. A third-party guide names QAD, Plex and Epicor Kinetic as the automotive picks. NetSuite and Business Central reach automotive through partners.

criterion: Implementation partners within reach of Ohio
why: Business Central is only sold through partners and there are many of them. Plex has the smallest partner bench of the four.
Oracle and Microsoft are not going anywhere. Plex is owned by Rockwell Automation. Epicor is a large private company.

criterion: Ease of use for office and floor staff
why: A third-party review calls Plex easy to navigate. Kinetic is midway through moving its screens to a new interface. NetSuite and Business Central are my judgment.

criterion: Five-year cost (calculated on the Cost sheet)
why: Scored by formula: 5 times the cheapest five-year cost, divided by this vendor's. Only Business Central publishes its prices. The other three are third-party starting prices plus my assumptions.
Microsoft publishes Business Central's price per user. Oracle has no public price list for NetSuite. Epicor and Plex both price by quote.
